title: Counit-normalized clopen exceptional comparisons and finite evaluation
statement:
Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, its valuation ring $O=\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and $A_n=O/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\geq1$ [def-pur-conventions]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be separated of finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, without assuming $Y$ separated over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $I$ be finite and let $j_i:X_i\hookrightarrow X$ be pairwise disjoint open and closed immersions covering $X$, with $g_i=g\circ j_i$ [def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Empty components and the empty cover of $X=\varnothing$ are allowed.

Fix $c=(a,p)$, $c_i=(a\circ j_i,p)$ [def-weil-compactifications-refinements]. At each positive finite coefficient level on the pro-etale site, use restriction $r_i$, zero insertion $E_i$, their adjunction counit $c_i^{\mathrm{ins}}:E_ir_i\to\mathrm{id}$ and the normalized compact-support isomorphism $b_i:F_gE_i\cong F_{g_i}$ of [lem-pur-clopen-common-compact-support]. Let $G_g=Rg_n^!$ and $G_{g_i}=R(g_i)_n^!$ be the constructible exceptional functors, with their finite etale-origin adjunction counits $\varepsilon_g,\varepsilon_{g_i}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. There is a unique natural isomorphism $\rho_{i,n}:r_iG_g\cong G_{g_i}$ satisfying
$$\varepsilon_{g_i,L}\circ F_{g_i}(\rho_{i,n,L})=
\varepsilon_{g,L}\circ F_g(c^{\mathrm{ins}}_{i,G_gL})\circ b_{i,r_iG_gL}^{-1}.$$
It represents the natural Hom bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(M,r_iG_gL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_iM,G_gL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{g_i}M,L)$ inside the full bounded constructible category. It is the component right-adjoint comparison of the finite compact-support direct-sum decomposition, compatibly with canonical compactification comparisons.

On the actual derived categories $D(\mathsf S_A(T_{\mathrm{et}}))$ of strict varying-coefficient systems, let $r_{i,A},E_{i,A},F_{g,A},F_{g_i,A},b_{i,A}$ and their insertion counit be those of [lem-pur-clopen-strict-system-support]. Let $G_{g,A},G_{g_i,A}$ be the actual $O$-linear right adjoints of these $F$ functors [lem-pur-etale-coefficient-system-adjoint]. There is a unique natural isomorphism
$$\rho_{i,A}:r_{i,A}G_{g,A}\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{g_i,A}$$
satisfying the same counit equation with system subscripts. It is an isomorphism of functors of derived strict systems, $O$-linear on morphisms. Evaluation of this equation, including the insertion and exceptional adjunction counits, identifies $e_n\rho_{i,A}$ with the ordinary etale finite-level counit-normalized right-adjoint comparison for every $n$. These comparisons respect quotient transitions with their prescribed adjunction mates; no faithfulness of evaluations on arbitrary derived-system morphisms is assumed.

source.place: Right adjoint $Rf^{N!}$ defined after Lemma 5.16 (Brown representability), and Lemma 5.22 (evaluation of $Rf^{N!}$), printed pp. 35-36. Argument: former Steps 4 and 7 of lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction, retained verbatim in coord/reports/Q121/lem-pur-finite-clopen-exceptional-restriction.md

proof.text:
At fixed $n$, set $H=r_iG_g$. The common-support lemma gives $E_i\dashv r_i$, preservation of bounded constructibility by $E_i$, and $b_i:F_gE_i\cong F_{g_i}$. The exceptional-image definition places $G_gL,G_{g_i}L$ in the bounded constructible categories. The class adjunction theorem supplies the exceptional Hom bijection for $E_iM$: its statement explicitly includes bounded constructible inputs. Hence, for $M\in D^b_c(X_i,A_n)$ and $L\in D^b_c(Y,A_n)$, compose the natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,HL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(E_iM,G_gL)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_gE_iM,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(F_{g_i}M,L).$$
The last bijection sends $v:F_gE_iM\to L$ to $v\circ b_{i,M}^{-1}$. This uses precisely the chosen compactification and the specified $b_i$. Restriction $r_i$ preserves bounded constructibility because the finite-clopen equivalence restricts to $D^b_c(X,A_n)\simeq\prod_iD^b_c(X_i,A_n)$ [lem-pur-finite-clopen-derived-decomposition], so both representing objects lie in the full category where these Hom sets are taken. No adjunction on arbitrary pro-etale objects is needed.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text:
The composite-adjunction counit formula says that the Hom bijection of Step 1 makes $H$ right adjoint to $F_{g_i}$ with counit
$$q_{i,L}=\varepsilon_{g,L}\circ F_g(c^{\mathrm{ins}}_{i,G_gL})\circ b_{i,HL}^{-1}.$$
Indeed the identity of $HL$ first transposes to $c^{\mathrm{ins}}_{i,G_gL}$, then to its image under $F_g$ followed by $\varepsilon_{g,L}$, and finally is precomposed with $b_{i,HL}^{-1}$. Apply counit-compatible uniqueness of right adjoints to this adjunction and $F_{g_i}\dashv G_{g_i}$. It gives the natural isomorphism $\rho_{i,n}:H\cong G_{g_i}$ and exactly $\varepsilon_{g_i,L}F_{g_i}(\rho_{i,n,L})=q_{i,L}$, uniquely even among families satisfying this equation. Its Hom representation is the composite of Step 1.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text: The finite sum comparison of the common-support lemma is the image of $K\cong\bigoplus_iE_ir_iK$. Its $i$-th inclusion, after $b_i^{-1}$, is $F_g(c^{\mathrm{ins}}_{i,K})$. At $K=G_gL$, followed by $\varepsilon_{g,L}$, this is exactly $q_{i,L}$. Thus the component right-adjoint comparison of that sum is the one fixed in Step 2. For a canonical change of compactification the common-support lemma identifies the left comparisons and the class adjunction theorem identifies the Hom bijections. Transposing either composite therefore gives the same $q_{i,L}$; uniqueness in Step 2 identifies the right comparisons. The same reasoning for successive changes proves the cocycle compatibility, because the cited left and Hom comparisons satisfy it.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text:
Now use the actual derived strict-system categories. The strict-support lemma gives $E_{i,A}\dashv r_{i,A}$ with its specified insertion counit and $b_{i,A}:F_{g,A}E_{i,A}\cong F_{g_i,A}$. The system-adjoint lemma gives $F_{g,A}\dashv G_{g,A}$ and $F_{g_i,A}\dashv G_{g_i,A}$. Compose the first two Hom bijections and precompose with $b_{i,A}^{-1}$, exactly as in Step 1, now for arbitrary derived strict systems $M,N$. The composite-adjunction formula gives the counit
$$q_{i,A,N}=\varepsilon_{g,A,N}\circ F_{g,A}(c^{\mathrm{ins}}_{i,A,G_{g,A}N})\circ b_{i,A,r_{i,A}G_{g,A}N}^{-1}.$$
Counit-compatible uniqueness produces $\rho_{i,A}:r_{i,A}G_{g,A}\cong G_{g_i,A}$ in these categories, uniquely with $\varepsilon_{g_i,A}F_{g_i,A}(\rho_{i,A})=q_{i,A}$. This constructs a natural transformation on derived systems themselves, before evaluation.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text:
Write $H_A=r_{i,A}G_{g,A}$ and let $\eta_{g_i,A}$ be the unit of $F_{g_i,A}\dashv G_{g_i,A}$. Explicitly, by the conjugate/transpose formula,
$$\rho_{i,A,N}=G_{g_i,A}(q_{i,A,N})\circ\eta_{g_i,A,H_AN}.$$
The system-adjoint lemma makes $G_{g,A}$ and $G_{g_i,A}$ $O$-linear. Restriction is componentwise, hence $O$-linear on morphisms, so $H_A$ is $O$-linear too. In particular for $a\in O$ and $u:N\to N'$,
$$G_{g_i,A}(au)\circ\rho_{i,A,N}=a\bigl(G_{g_i,A}(u)\circ\rho_{i,A,N}\bigr)=a\bigl(\rho_{i,A,N'}\circ H_A(u)\bigr)=\rho_{i,A,N'}\circ H_A(au).$$
Thus this natural isomorphism is between $O$-linear functors and respects their linear map actions; no choice of component maps is involved.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text:
Evaluation commutes with restriction, insertion, $b_{i,A}$ and the insertion counit by the strict-support lemma. The system-adjoint lemma identifies $e_nG_{f,A}$ with $f_n^\times e_n$ and identifies evaluated units and counits with the finite etale ones. Evaluate the explicit formula in Step 5. After these specified identifications it becomes
$$e_n\rho_{i,A,N}=(g_i)_n^\times(e_nq_{i,A,N})\circ\eta_{g_i,n,r_i g_n^\times(e_nN)}.$$
Every factor in $e_nq_{i,A,N}$ is the corresponding ordinary etale factor at level $n$: the evaluated insertion counit, $F_g$, $b_{i,n}$ and the etale counit $\varepsilon_{g,n}$ of the formula of Step 4. Consequently this formula is precisely the finite etale transpose of its normalized counit, and the uniqueness lemma identifies it with the ordinary etale finite-level comparison at $e_nN$. This is an equality of evaluated maps, using the evaluated unit as well as the counit, and is natural in $N$.

source.place: Brown right adjoint following Lemma 5.16 and evaluation Lemma 5.22, printed pp. 35–36; component argument from the retained Q121 proof, old steps 4 and 7.

proof.text: For a quotient $A_m\to A_n$, the strict-support compositor and insertion maps commute with the actual coefficient transitions. The system-adjoint comparisons identify the exceptional transitions with their prescribed adjunction mates. Apply mate pasting to the composite adjunction used in Step 4: its quotient comparison is the composite of the restriction/insertion mate and the exceptional mate. Since $b_{i,A}$ commutes with transitions, changing the left adjunction by $b_{i,A}^{-1}$ gives the same pasted mate (clause 3 of the pasting lemma). Its conjugate is exactly $\rho_{i,A}$ by Step 5. This proves the quotient-transition square for $\rho_{i,A}$, including successive quotients by clauses 1–2 of mate pasting. The identity quotient uses clause 4. These are mates of the actual system maps; no assertion that all evaluations jointly detect derived morphism equalities is used. If $X_i$ is empty, the component category is zero and all these identities are its unique identities. If $I$ is empty there are no indices or comparisons and the sum of Step 3 is the zero functor, as the two support lemmas specify.
